# `nish/compress/deflate`

DEFLATE (RFC 1951), both ways, in pure Nish: a compressor with levels and a decompressor that refuses malformed input with an error code. `nish/compress/gzip` and `nish/compress/zlib` frame it.

```ts
import {
  DEFLATE_BEST,
  DEFLATE_DEFAULT,
  DEFLATE_ERR_BLOCK_TYPE,
  DEFLATE_ERR_DISTANCE,
  DEFLATE_ERR_HUFFMAN,
  DEFLATE_ERR_OUTPUT_LIMIT,
  DEFLATE_ERR_STORED_LENGTH,
  DEFLATE_ERR_SYMBOL,
  DEFLATE_ERR_TRAILING,
  DEFLATE_ERR_TRUNCATED,
  DEFLATE_FAST,
  DEFLATE_NO_ROOM,
  DEFLATE_STORE,
  DeflateHuffmanScratch,
  Deflater,
  FixedDeflater,
  INFLATE_DONE,
  INFLATE_NEED_INPUT,
  INFLATE_NEED_OUTPUT,
  InflateTable,
  Inflater,
  compressBound,
  deflateBound,
  deflateCompress,
  deflateDecompress,
  fixedDeflateBound,
} from "nish/compress/deflate";
```

```ts
import { Deflater, Inflater, DEFLATE_FAST, deflateBound } from "nish/compress/deflate";

const deflater = new Deflater(DEFLATE_FAST); // tables, once
const out: u8[] = new Array<u8>(deflateBound(len));
const end: i32 = deflater.compress(src, off, len, out, 0); // -1: no room
const inflater = new Inflater();
const n: i32 = inflater.decompress(out, 0, end, back, 0, limit); // < 0: an error
```

<scalar-detail title="Sans-IO and allocation-free once built">

Both objects take caller-owned
windows, `src[off .. off + len)` in and `out[at ..)` out, and answer where
the output ends. Everything a call needs — the match finder's hash chains,
the block's symbols, the Huffman scratch, the decoder's tables — is
allocated by the constructor, about 330 KB for a `Deflater` and 28 KB for an
`Inflater`, so build one per thread and reuse it: a call allocates nothing.
The free functions `deflateCompress` and `deflateDecompress` build one for
a single call, for a program that compresses once.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Levels">

`DEFLATE_STORE` (0) writes stored blocks only. 1 to 3 match
greedily on a four-byte hash with a short chain (`DEFLATE_FAST` is 1, about
libdeflate's level 1); 4 to 9 match lazily on a three-byte hash with longer
chains (`DEFLATE_DEFAULT` is 6). Every block is written as whichever of
dynamic Huffman, fixed Huffman and stored is smallest, by its exact size in
bits, so no level ever expands its input by more than `deflateBound`
allows. A block ends after 16,383 symbols.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Decompression is bounded and total">

`Inflater.decompress` writes at most
`limit` bytes, and a stream that would write more answers
`DEFLATE_ERR_OUTPUT_LIMIT`, so a small input cannot expand without bound.
Every malformed stream — a reserved block type, a stored length whose
complement is wrong, an over-subscribed or incomplete code, a symbol no code
defines, a distance before the start of the output, input that ends inside
the stream — answers its own negative `DEFLATE_ERR_*` code; nothing a stream
holds can panic. Bytes after the final block are `DEFLATE_ERR_TRAILING`
from `decompress`; `inflate`, the resumable step under it and
`nish/compress/gzip`'s reader, stops at the final block and says where.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="What is unchecked">

The hot loops read and write through `nish:unsafe`'s
`uncheckedGet` and `uncheckedSet`. Each such index is one of: a table
entry, below a size the constructor allocated and the `readonly` field
keeps; a position the caller's window was checked to contain before the
loop; or a match candidate, which the loop checks lies in
`[histStart, p)` before reading it. A stream's distances and lengths are
checked against the output before any copy.

</scalar-detail>

Written from RFC 1951; the code-length construction follows Moffat and
Katajainen, "In-place calculation of minimum-redundancy codes" (1995), and
the length limit is the Kraft-sum repair of the counts per length. Not
ported from another implementation.

## compressBound

The most bytes a compressed body of `n` input bytes takes in any of this
directory's formats: `deflateBound(n)` with room for gzip's 18 bytes of
header and trailer, which covers zlib's 6.

```ts
function compressBound(n: i32): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="n" type="i32" required>

The length of the input, in bytes.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

A size in bytes, not a position: an `out` with this many bytes
  from `at` always holds the raw, zlib or gzip stream.

</scalar-field>

## deflateBound

The most bytes `Deflater.compress` writes for `n` bytes of input, at any
level: the input stored, five bytes of framing for every 65,535 and for
every block, and slack for the last partial byte. `n` is at most
2^31 - 1 less the framing; a negative `n` answers 0.

```ts
function deflateBound(n: i32): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="n" type="i32" required>

The length of the input, in bytes.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

A size in bytes, not a position: an `out` with this many bytes
  from `at` always holds the stream.

</scalar-field>

## deflateCompress

`Deflater.compress` at `level`, building the compressor for this call
alone: 330 KB allocated and filled each time, so keep a `Deflater` for
anything repeated.

```ts
function deflateCompress(
  src: u8[],
  off: i32,
  len: i32,
  out: u8[],
  at: i32,
  level: i32,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="src" type="u8[]" required>

The array that holds the data to compress.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where in `src` the data starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="len" type="i32" required>

How many bytes of data to compress.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="out" type="u8[]" required>

The caller's array the stream is written into.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="at" type="i32" required>

Where in `out` the stream starts.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="level" type="i32" required>

How hard to compress, 0 to 9; another level panics.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

The index in `out` one past the stream's last byte, or
  `DEFLATE_NO_ROOM`, as `Deflater.compress` answers.

</scalar-field>

## fixedDeflateBound

The most bytes `FixedDeflater.compress` writes for `n` bytes of input: nine
bits a byte, the block's header and end code, and the eight bytes of slack
its word-wide bit writer stores past the last whole byte. A negative `n`
answers the bound of 0.

```ts
function fixedDeflateBound(n: i32): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="n" type="i32" required>

The length of the input, in bytes.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

A size in bytes, not a position: a `room` of this many always
  holds the block.

</scalar-field>

## DeflateHuffmanScratch

The scratch `deflateLengths` sorts and folds in, sized for the 288
literal/length symbols, the largest alphabet.

```ts
class DeflateHuffmanScratch
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |

## Deflater

A DEFLATE compressor at one level: the match finder's tables, one block of
symbols, the Huffman scratch and the bit writer, allocated once. Not shared
between threads; reuse it for every call on one.

```ts
class Deflater
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Deflater(level: i32)` | A compressor at `level`, 0 to 9; another level panics. |
| `compress(src: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, out: u8[], at: i32): i32` | Compresses `src[off .. off + len)` into `out` from `at` as one raw DEFLATE stream, and answers where it ends, or `DEFLATE_NO_ROOM` when `out` cannot hold it: `deflateBound(len)` bytes always can. A window outside its array panics. Allocates nothing. |

## FixedDeflater

A one-block DEFLATE compressor in the fixed Huffman code (BTYPE=01, §3.2.6)
for short inputs such as an HTTP response body: one hash probe per position,
matches at most `FIXED_WINDOW` back, no code to build or send. It carries
nothing from one call to the next: the hash table, sized to the input, is
cleared at the start of every call, so the output is a function of the
input alone. About 70 KB of tables; reuse one per thread.

```ts
class FixedDeflater
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new FixedDeflater()` | The tables, once. |
| `compress(src: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, out: u8[], at: i32, room: i32): i32` | Compresses `src[off .. off + len)` as one final fixed-Huffman block into `out[at .. at + room)`, and answers where it ends, or `DEFLATE_NO_ROOM` as soon as it would need more than `room` bytes: a caller that only wants the output when it is smaller passes the most it will take, and an input that does not compress is abandoned part way. `fixedDeflateBound(len)` always fits. A window outside its array panics. Allocates nothing. |

## InflateTable

One Huffman decoding table: the entries for every `bits`-bit prefix, and
for the codes longer than that, the count per length and the symbols in
canonical order that a bit-at-a-time decode walks (§3.2.2).

```ts
class InflateTable
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new InflateTable(bits: i32, symbols: i32, capacity: i32)` | A table indexing `bits` bits, for an alphabet of up to `symbols` symbols, with room for `capacity` entries: the main table and its subtables. The arrays are allocated here and filled by `Inflater`. |

## Inflater

A DEFLATE decompressor: the decoding tables, the fixed code's, and the state
that lets `inflate` stop at the end of its input or output and resume.
Not shared between threads.

```ts
class Inflater
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new Inflater()` | Builds the tables, the fixed code's among them. |
| `consumed: i32` | The input bytes the last `decompress` read, its final block included. |
| `inPos: i32` | Where the last `inflate` stopped in its input: the first byte it did not use, or after `INFLATE_DONE` the first byte after the final block. |
| `outPos: i32` | Where the last `inflate` stopped in its output: one past the last byte it wrote. |
| `decompress(src: u8[], off: i32, len: i32, out: u8[], at: i32, limit: i32): i32` | Decompresses the raw DEFLATE stream `src[off .. off + len)` into `out` from `at`, writing at most `limit` bytes and never past `out`'s end, and answers where the output ends; or `DEFLATE_ERR_OUTPUT_LIMIT` when the stream holds more, `DEFLATE_ERR_TRAILING` when bytes follow its final block, or another negative `DEFLATE_ERR_*` for a malformed stream. A window outside its array, or a negative `limit`, panics. Allocates nothing. |
| `inflate(src: u8[], ip: i32, inEnd: i32, more: boolean, out: u8[], op: i32, outEnd: i32, histStart: i32): i32` | Decodes from `src[ip .. inEnd)` into `out[op .. outEnd)`, resuming where the last call stopped: the resumable step under `decompress`, for a stream that arrives in pieces or an output buffer that is drained between calls. `GzipDecompressor`, `GzipReader` and `ZlibDecompressor` are built on it. `inPos` and `outPos` say where it stopped. Windows outside their arrays panic. Allocates nothing. |
| `reset(): void` | Starts a new stream: the next `inflate` reads a first block header and whatever the last stream left in the bit buffer is dropped. A new `Inflater` is already at the start, and `decompress` resets itself; call this before reusing one for another stream through `inflate`. |

## Constants

<scalar-grid cols="2">

<scalar-card title="9" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_BEST: i32`

Level 9: lazy matching on the longest chains.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_DEFAULT: i32`

Level 6: lazy matching, zlib's and gzip's default balance.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_ERR_BLOCK_TYPE: i32`

A block of the reserved type 3 (RFC 1951 §3.2.3).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-7" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_ERR_DISTANCE: i32`

A distance that reaches back before the start of the output.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-5" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_ERR_HUFFMAN: i32`

A dynamic block's code is unusable (§3.2.7): an over-subscribed or
incomplete set of lengths, a repeat with nothing to repeat or past the end,
more than 286 literal/length or 30 distance codes, or no end-of-block code.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-8" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_ERR_OUTPUT_LIMIT: i32`

The output would pass `limit` bytes, or the end of `out`.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-4" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_ERR_STORED_LENGTH: i32`

A stored block whose `NLEN` is not the complement of its `LEN` (§3.2.4).

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-6" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_ERR_SYMBOL: i32`

A code the block's tables do not define, or literal/length 286 or 287, or distance 30 or 31.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-15" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_ERR_TRAILING: i32`

`decompress`: bytes follow the final block.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_ERR_TRUNCATED: i32`

The input ends inside the stream.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_FAST: i32`

Level 1: greedy matching on a short hash chain, for speed over ratio.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="-1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_NO_ROOM: i32`

`compress` and its framings: `out` has no room for the whole stream.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="0" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`DEFLATE_STORE: i32`

Level 0: stored blocks only, the input copied with five bytes of framing per 65,535.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="1" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`INFLATE_DONE: i32`

`Inflater.inflate`: the final block has ended; `inPos` is the first byte after it.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="2" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`INFLATE_NEED_INPUT: i32`

`Inflater.inflate`: every byte given was used and the stream goes on; call again with more.

</scalar-card>

<scalar-card title="3" icon="phosphor/regular/hash">

`INFLATE_NEED_OUTPUT: i32`

`Inflater.inflate`: the next symbol does not fit before `outEnd`; make room and call again.

</scalar-card>

</scalar-grid>
